The test performs two distinct 'Act' operations: g.numVertices() and g.existeAresta(0,0). Decision rule 1 flags >1 method calls as non-compliant because it does not focus on a single behavior per test.

The test uses only local variables and no shared mutable state; there are no @Before/@After but the method does not rely on external/stateful fixtures. Decision rule 4 indicates compliant when only local variables are used.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: Only a happy-path assertion is present (and a safe existence check). The class has a single test method and contains no tests for error/exceptional flows (no @Test(expected=...) or assertThrows). Decision rule 4 marks this non-compliant.
The test constructs a graph with 0 vertices and uses index 0 for existence checks, explicitly testing the empty/zero boundary. This matches the evaluation criteria for boundary value checks.

There are no helper methods or constants and the test uses hard-coded setup values; although only one test exists (so duplication isn't visible), the lack of modular helpers or constants indicates non-compliant per rules.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The test method is small, linear, and contains no loops or complex conditionals; it appears below the 20-line threshold and follows a simple Arrange-Act-Assert flow, meeting the compliant criteria.
The test asserts two different properties (numVertices value and existence check), providing more than one assertion which improves fault detection beyond a single superficial assertion.
No @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out @Test lines are present; tests are active and runnable, satisfying the maintenance practice.
The test includes an inline comment referencing a requirement ID 'REQ-GRAPH-009', providing direct traceability to a requirement per the evaluation criteria.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: The test method includes an explicit @Test(timeout = 4000) annotation which is an explicit timing-related check; per decision rules this satisfies the practice and is marked compliant.
The method name is 'test08', which is generic and does not follow descriptive naming conventions like method_condition_expectedResult. Decision rule 2 indicates non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: The file contains signs of test-generation provenance (EvoSuite imports and preserved test name pattern 'test08'), and method names appear auto-generated rather than intention-revealing; decision rules flag heavy generation patterns as non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The test contains Given-When-Then comments and a focused scenario, indicating a designed test structure consistent with BDD/Given-When-Then intent per decision rule 1.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts only with public API (Grafo constructor and public methods) and does not use reflection or inspect private state, meeting the criteria for maintainable behavior-focused tests.
Assertions are specific (assertEquals, assertFalse) and include descriptive failure messages for at least one assertion; generic assertTrue is not used, matching the guidance.
The test uses concise Given-When-Then comments and a short class-level Javadoc; comments explain intent rather than restating obvious code, complying with the practice.
The test does not use random values, current time, thread sleeps, or external dependencies; it should produce deterministic results when run, satisfying the practice.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test only creates a local Grafo instance and performs in-memory checks without persisting data or modifying static state; no cleanup is required and no side-effects are observed.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class) and defines a UnitTest marker interface, meeting the labeling/categorization criteria.

The test performs a single primary 'Act' operation (g.insereAresta(...)) followed by assertions verifying result. There is one clear Arrange-Act-Assert flow focused on the behavior of inserting an edge into a zero-vertex graph.
The test uses only local variables (Grafo g) and does not reference or modify any static/instance state. No setup/teardown annotations are required for this single, self-contained test.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: The class contains only this single test method and it exercises a single (mostly happy-path) scenario. There is no complementary test in the class for an error/exception flow of the same operation, and the class has fewer than two test methods overall.
The test constructs a zero-vertex graph (Grafo(0)) and attempts to insert edges using negative indices, explicitly exercising boundary/edge conditions (empty graph and negative indices).
The test is short and self-contained (no repeated setup), so lack of helper methods is acceptable. There is no duplication within the single method and it follows a clear Arrange-Act-Assert pattern.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The test method is small (well under 20-30 lines), has no loops or nested conditionals, and follows a straight-line Arrange-Act-Assert flow, indicating low cyclomatic complexity.

The test contains effectively a single meaningful assertion (numVertices == 0) and a fail() in a catch; it does not verify multiple distinct properties of the result/object (only one property is asserted), which limits fault-detection capability.
There are no @Ignore/@Disabled annotations, no commented-out @Test methods, and no TODO markers in the provided method; the test appears active and runnable.
The test includes an explicit requirement identifier in a comment ("REQ-GRAPH-008:"), providing traceability to a requirement.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses a timeout on the @Test annotation (timeout = 4000), providing an explicit performance-related assertion (execution time bound). This is an explicit performance/test constraint in the test.

The method name 'test07' is generic and does not describe the scenario or expected outcome. Although comments describe the intent, the name itself does not follow descriptive naming conventions (methodName_scenario_expectedResult).

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: The file imports EvoSuite runtime classes and uses a generated-style method name ('test07'), which are signals of test generation tooling. These patterns indicate generated-style naming/artifacts rather than minimal, intention-revealing tests.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The test contains Given-When-Then style comments and demonstrates a clear design intent. The presence of explicit scenario comments indicates thoughtful design rather than an ad-hoc one-liner.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts only with the public API (constructor, insereAresta, numVertices). There is no reflection or access to internal/private state, indicating a behavior-focused design.
Assertions include descriptive failure messages (assertEquals with message, fail with explanatory message). Specific assertion methods (assertEquals) are used rather than generic asserts only.

The method includes concise Given-When-Then comments that explain intent (why the test exists). There is no excessive or commented-out code; comments add value by documenting the requirement being tested.
The test contains no sources of non-determinism (no Random, no use of current time, no Thread.sleep). It uses only deterministic operations on a local Grafo instance.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
